evals.name: poster-grid-image-sizing-and-placeholders
evals.prompt: This poster grid works on my laptop but on a 2020 smart TV the cells stay blank while I scroll, images fade in slowly, and after browsing a few categories the app crashes. The `artworkUrl` points at our image service which returns a 2000x3000 master but also accepts `?w=` and `?h=` resize params. Fix the component so it behaves on the TV. `poster-grid.js` and `_framework.md` (the tiny fixture framework) are attached.
evals.expected_output: Requests a CDN/image-service rendition sized to the 260x390 cell (roughly, accounting for the 1080p UI — not the 2000x3000 master) via the ?w=/?h= params instead of passing the raw master URL. Adds a cheap placeholder (solid rect / one shared tiny texture) shown while the image loads and on failure, rather than a blank hole or a second image request. Explains the mechanism: decode CPU and texture memory are paid at the source pixel size, so a 2000x3000 image in a 260x390 slot is ~24MB of texture for one poster and blows the tens-of-MB texture budget after a few screens. Ideally notes that only the on-screen window of posters should hold textures at all (ties to virtualization) but the core ask is sizing + placeholders.
assertions: The image request is changed to ask the image service for a rendition sized to the on-screen cell (uses the ?w=/?h= resize params), not the raw 2000x3000 master URL
A cheap placeholder (solid color rect or one shared tiny texture) is shown while the image loads AND on load failure, never a blank gap or a second full image request per slot
The answer explains that decode cost and texture memory are paid at the SOURCE image's pixel size regardless of the display size, so oversized images exhaust the GPU texture budget
The answer references a concrete TV texture/RAM budget (e.g. tens of MB for all textures, ~1GB shared RAM, low-RAM device class) rather than treating memory as unbounded
No suggestion relies on desktop-class headroom (e.g. 'just preload all images', 'increase the cache size') without the sizing fix

evals.name: catalog-list-virtualization
evals.prompt: Our 'Browse all' screen renders the whole catalog (usually 400-800 titles) as one long scrolling list of rows. It takes several seconds to open on a TV and memory climbs the entire time the user scrolls down, and never drops when they scroll back up. How should this be built instead? `catalog-screen.js` and `_framework.md` are attached.
evals.expected_output: Introduces virtualization/windowing: only rows within (roughly) the viewport plus a small buffer are realized as nodes/textures; rows far from the viewport are not created or are released. Recommends recycling row/tile views as the window moves rather than building all of them. Explains that the full catalog should live as data while only a window exists as views and textures, and that leaving the viewport must release textures/images so memory plateaus during a long scroll instead of climbing. Bounds the realized set to about two screens. May mention pagination of the data and startup render order (first screen first).
assertions: The redesign only realizes rows/tiles near the viewport (a window plus small buffer), not the entire catalog at mount
Rows/tiles that scroll far from the viewport are released or recycled (their textures/images freed), so memory plateaus rather than climbing during a long scroll
The answer distinguishes the full catalog as data from the small window that exists as realized views/textures
View recycling / pooling of row or tile nodes is recommended rather than creating and destroying a node per item on every scroll step
The realized window is bounded to roughly one-to-two screens (an explicit small buffer), not an unbounded 'render what's been seen so far'

evals.name: hero-carousel-per-frame-allocation
evals.prompt: The home-screen hero carousel cross-fades between featured titles on a per-frame loop. On a TV the fade stutters and the whole home screen hitches each time it advances; on my laptop it's smooth. What's making it janky and how do I fix it? `hero-carousel.js` and `_framework.md` are attached.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the per-frame `step()` allocates every frame: `{ value: ... }` object, `this.slides.map(...).filter(...)` building a new array (and spread-cloning every slide object) each tick. That allocation churn drives GC pauses that show up as jank on a low-end TV even though the dev machine absorbs it. Fix: hoist/reuse scratch state, index into `this.slides` directly instead of map+filter, no object/array/closure construction inside the loop. Also flags that swapping the image `src` mid-fade forces a texture upload every advance (should preload/keep both slide textures and only animate alpha), and that only cheap properties (opacity/transform) should be animated per frame. Ideally notes a time-based delta rather than a fixed 0.08 step tied to frame rate.
assertions: Identifies the per-frame allocations in step(): the { value: ... } object, and the this.slides.map(...).filter(...) chain that builds a new array and spread-clones slide objects every frame
Explains that per-frame allocation creates GC pressure that manifests as jank/stutter on low-end TV hardware while being invisible on a dev machine
The fix removes allocation from the loop: reuse hoisted scratch values and index into this.slides directly (e.g. this.slides[this.current]) instead of map+filter

Notes that only cheap properties (opacity / transform) should be animated per frame, and/or that reassigning the image src mid-fade forces a texture re-upload each advance so both slide textures should be kept/preloaded
Does not misattribute the jank solely to the fade math constant or to needing a faster device, without addressing the allocation in the frame loop
